samples.summary: `--round N` walks straight past the self-review bound: the refusal is measured on the number the caller supplied, not on the rounds already on disk
samples.evidence: `const round = args.round === undefined ? nextRound(onDisk) : Number(args.round);` (line 958) then `const spentRound = args.fresh ? Math.max(round, nextRound(onDiskBefore)) : round;` (line 966). The `--fresh` renumbering hole was deliberately closed by measuring against `onDiskBefore`, but the identical hole via `--round` was not: with three real rounds on disk, `review --round 3` (or `--round 1`) yields `spentRound <= MAX_SELF_REVIEW_ROUNDS`, `roundBoundNotice` returns "", the refusal never fires and a fourth (fifth, …) real review round runs with no `--force` and no notice. The docblock at lines 216-236 states the bound is enforced and that `--force` is the only door, and the test `review --fresh cannot walk past the bound by renumbering to round 1` asserts exactly this property for the other flag. The same call also re-uses an existing round directory, so round 3's verdicts are overwritten by the new run. Fix is symmetric: `const spentRound = Math.max(round, nextRound(onDiskBefore))` in both branches.

samples.summary: `--dry-run --fresh --round N` (N>1) reports a carry-forward the real run would have deleted
samples.evidence: The dry-run branch computes `const dryPrior = round > 1 ? priorFindingsFor(base, round) : [];` (line 1002) without accounting for the `--fresh` deletion, which the real run performs at lines 988-992 *before* computing `prior` at line 1034. With `--fresh` alone the round is 1 so both are empty, but `--fresh --round 2 --force --dry-run` prints `[dry-run] carrying N prior finding(s) from earlier rounds` while the real run deletes every round directory first and carries 0. This is the same class of defect the rebuttals validation was added to prevent ("a dry run that announced it would adjudicate a file the real run rejects is the one answer this mode must never give", lines 1003-1006).

samples.summary: A re-used round number writes into the previous attempt's directory without clearing it, so stale per-lens verdicts survive and are read back as this round's
samples.evidence: `nextRound` deliberately re-uses a number when the previous attempt settled no lens (lines 166-186, the 429 case), and `--round N` can name any existing round; `mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` at line 1020 then reuses that directory as the panel's `--out` without removing what is already in it. If the retry's panel crashes partway (cmdReview then fails at line 1078), the earlier attempt's `<lens>/verdict.json` files remain; `roundsOnDisk`/`priorFindingsFor` (lines 811-849) cannot distinguish them from verdicts this round produced, so a later round can carry forward findings from a tree that has since been rewritten, or count a round as having reviewed when it did not.

samples.summary: `carryForwardFindings` claims to project but passes `mergedFrom`, `searchedFor` and `evidence` through by reference, unprojected and uncapped
samples.evidence: Lines 171-174 keep `evidence: f.evidence`, `searchedFor: Array.isArray(f.searchedFor) ? f.searchedFor : undefined` and `mergedFrom: Array.isArray(f.mergedFrom) ? f.mergedFrom : undefined` as-is, while the cloud copy this is said to mirror (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1028) rebuilds each `mergedFrom` member as `{severity, summary, adjudication:{upheld}}`, caps it at 5, and filters `searchedFor` to non-empty strings capped at 20. So the local carry-forward re-admits arbitrary model-written keys one level down — including a nested `infra: true`, which `isInfraRecord` only inspects at the top level — into the next round's verifier input, which is precisely what the "PROJECT, never spread" comment at lines 160-165 says must not happen. No crash results (review-panel.mjs:2137 re-filters `searchedFor`), so the impact is contained to prompt contents and unbounded size.

samples.summary: `roundsOnDisk`'s top-level `readdirSync(base)` is unguarded, so `priorFindingsFor`'s documented "never throws" contract can be violated
samples.evidence: Line 812 `return roundsIn(readdirSync(base)).map(...)` has no try/catch, while every other read on the path is guarded (lines 815-825, 843-846) and `priorFindingsFor`'s docblock (lines 832-838) states it never throws. If the base disappears or becomes unreadable between creation and the read (a concurrent `--fresh` run on the same branch shares the same deterministic base from `reviewBase`, and `rmSync` there removes directories under it), the call escapes as an uncaught ENOENT/EACCES stack rather than degrading to "carry nothing", which is the documented fail direction for this path.

samples.summary: The blocking-report footer tells the developer to re-run "for round N+1" even when the next run will re-use round N
samples.evidence: Line 1094 prints `then re-run for round ${round + 1}`, but `nextRound` (lines 180-186) deliberately re-uses the same number when the round settled no lens — the all-lenses-429 case the function documents. In that case the panel still exits 1 through this branch (every lens conclusion is `failure`), so the advice names a round number that will not be used.

samples.summary: The branch diff is captured through `execFileSync` with the default 1 MB `maxBuffer`, so a large branch fails the local review outright
samples.evidence: `writeFileSync(diffFile, execFileSync("git", ["diff", "origin/main...HEAD"], { encoding: "utf8" }))` (line 1045, pre-existing but now the sole review path for every ordinary feature branch) inherits Node's 1 MiB `maxBuffer`; a branch diff above that throws ENOBUFS and is reported as `could not build the working diff`, which names the wrong cause. It fails loudly rather than silently reviewing a truncated diff, hence the contained severity; `maxBuffer` should be raised or the diff redirected to the file by git itself.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. At spec-to-pr.mjs:958 an explicit `--round N` replaces the on-disk-derived round number, and at :966 the compensating `Math.max(round, nextRound(onDiskBefore))` is applied only in the `args.fresh` branch. With MAX_SELF_REVIEW_ROUNDS = 3 (:152) and three real rounds on disk, `review --round 3` (or `--round 1`) gives `spentRound <= max`, so `roundBoundNotice` returns "" (:229), the refusal at :968 never fires, and the `--force` warning at :976 never prints — a fourth+ real round runs silently past a bound the code itself documents as ENFORCED with `--force` as the only override (:151-152, :216-236). The only validation on `--round` is `reviewArgsError` (:605-615), which checks positive-integer only and never consults the bound or the rounds on disk, so no upstream guard makes this unreachable. The data-overwrite half is also real: after the gate, :994 and :1020 reuse the existing `round-N` directory and :1026/:1045-1046 point the panel's `--out` and diff writes at it, clobbering that round's verdicts. The parallel property is tested for `--fresh` (test.mjs:702-744, :746-781) but has no `--round` equivalent (:334 covers only the valueless-flag usage error). Reachable through the documented CLI surface (:30, :1112). Major: a bound bypass plus overwrite of a prior round's verdicts on a normal-use path.

finding.summary: `--fresh` deletes the rounds BEFORE the new bound refusal runs, so a refused run still destroys the carry-forward and the bound is bypassed by simply re-running
finding.evidence: In `cmdReview`, the delete loop `if (args.fresh && !dryRun) { for (const name of roundDirsToClear(readdirSync(base))) rmSync(...) }` (lines 954-958) executes BEFORE the bound decision at lines 974-983. On a real (non-dry) run with MAX rounds on disk, `spec-to-pr review --fresh` therefore: (1) removes every `round-N` directory, then (2) exits 1 with "past the self-review bound" — a command that reports it did nothing has already deleted the verdicts the message says must not be discarded. Worse, the state it measured is now gone: the very next invocation (with or without `--fresh`) sees `roundsOnDisk(base) === []`, so `onDiskBefore` is empty, `spentRound` is 1, `roundBoundNotice(1)` is "", and the round runs without `--force`. The new guard is thus defeated deterministically in one retry, which is exactly the "a fourth round presents itself as a clean first one" failure the comment at lines 967-973 claims to close. The added test only exercises `--dry-run` (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:657-700), where the delete is skipped, so this path is uncovered. Fix: compute `notice`/`spentRound` and refuse before performing the `--fresh` deletion.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the `--fresh` delete loop runs before the round-bound refusal. In the working tree the order is the opposite: `onDiskBefore = roundsOnDisk(base)` is read at spec-to-pr.mjs:949, `spentRound`/`notice` are computed at 966-967, the bound refusal `if (notice && !args.force) return fail(...)` is at 968-975, and the `--fresh` delete loop `if (args.fresh && !dryRun) { for (const name of roundDirsToClear(readdirSync(base))) rmSync(...) }` is at 988-992 — strictly after the refusal. Grep confirms `rmSync` occurs exactly once in executable code (line 990); there is no earlier deletion. Because the refusal is `return fail(...)`, a refused `--fresh` run never reaches the delete, leaves every round-N directory intact, and the next invocation still measures the same `onDiskBefore`, so the bound is not bypassed by re-running. The comments at 953-956 and 978-987 explicitly describe the reviewer's scenario as the defect this ordering avoids. The claimed defective code is not present as described (the finding's proposed fix is already what the file does); the dry-run-only test coverage point is moot since there is no destructive pre-refusal path to cover.
